title: Early Detection of Breast Cancer in MRI Using AI.
summary: A patient-level evaluated CNN predicts subsequent cancer risk from current MRI in a retrospective high-risk cohort. It is a single-site proof of concept with modest discrimination and low positive predictive value; the earliest located result-bearing version is the 2023 preprint.
ai_technology: A pretrained 2D CNN is fine-tuned using per-slice probabilities to predict one-year future cancer risk from current MRI; patient-level 10-fold evaluation avoids patient overlap between train/test.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: The retrospective 910-woman cohort (3,029 exams, 5,128 breasts, 115 later cancers) yielded reported AUC 0.72 and a top-risk selection with 35/115 cancers at 30% sensitivity; study is described as proof of concept.
evidence.unknown: Internal patient-level cross-validation with later cancer ascertainment; single-site retrospective cohort and low PPV/high false-discovery burden constrain use.
evidence.ai_role: A pretrained 2D CNN is fine-tuned using per-slice probabilities to predict one-year future cancer risk from current MRI; patient-level 10-fold evaluation avoids patient overlap between train/test.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
